ideas.risks: The formula may be a known robust-pricing special case rather than new; boundary cases delta*=c_i and strict crossing could hide epsilon losses; it remains purely local even if correct.
ideas.summary: Verify and package the solver's finite-C primal formula. For C={0<c_1<...<c_m}, check that the unique root delta* of F(delta)=1 really equals kappa(C), including m=1, delta*=0, delta*=c_i boundary cases, and left-limit actions. Then compare the q_i distribution to randomized minimax pricing formulas in Bergemann-Schlag-style prior-free pricing.
ideas.title: Promote Finite-C Primal Formula
ideas.why_promising: This directly closes the iteration-8 open item and gives an explicit local optimizer, not just a dual value. It can become a reusable lemma for both lower bounds and candidate upper bounds.

ideas.risks: Local block strategies may not compose because one fixed comparator spans multiple blocks and old quotes can fill at later records. Nonmonotone price paths may break the clean threshold-menu reduction.
ideas.summary: Try for a matching known-path anytime upper bound using the explicit local minimax mixtures. Model a deterministic known path by epochs whose future record thresholds form finite menus, choose q_i-style quote distributions on long unresolved stretches, and test whether every path admits limsup_T R_T/T <= 1/e or a sharper path-dependent local-density bound.
ideas.title: Known-Path Anytime Upper Bound
ideas.why_promising: The same-path lower bound now reaches 1/e, and the solver supplies the primal strategy that matches each isolated block. If these strategies compose, the process-aware horizon-oblivious regime could get a sharp characterization.

ideas.risks: Approachability may become infinite-dimensional as thresholds and horizons grow; feedback is horizon-censored; global comparator values may not decompose into local vector payoffs.
ideas.summary: Formulate horizon-oblivious learning on a known path as vector-deficit approachability. For a finite active threshold set C, define deficit coordinates against each prefix/comparator and use the solver's q_i as the one-shot minimax action. Explore whether Blackwell approachability or global-cost regret gives an anytime policy when the target set is approachable.
ideas.title: Vector Deficit Approachability
ideas.why_promising: It turns the informal 'one quote sequence serves many horizons' obstruction into a standard simultaneous-objective problem and may produce both algorithms and impossibility certificates.

ideas.risks: The construction can accidentally become hard in expectation if rare blocks are not predictable enough, or trivial if a process-aware learner can condition on the branch. Must avoid presenting the dual threshold law itself as the hard stochastic process.
ideas.summary: Build a rare-event process where, conditional on E_i, a long zero block is followed by an equal-revenue threshold menu with kappa close to 1/e, but P(E_i)N_i=o(T_i). Check that essential-sup tails and conditional local kappa stay large while expected regret remains o(T) for a process-aware or suitably informed learner.
ideas.title: Rare Event Kappa Stress Test
ideas.why_promising: This would strengthen CE-006 from a suggestion into a formal obstruction against any necessity condition based on essential sup or unweighted post-history hardness.

ideas.risks: The best truncation gap Gamma_T(H) may be unobservable; meta-learning across H has delayed/censored feedback; most arbitrary-delay literature is bandit/OCO rather than this full-information public-price reduction.
ideas.summary: Develop an oracle-free sufficiency theorem that competes with the best truncation scale H in hindsight: run multi-scale truncated grid learners, skip fills unresolved after H, and aim for regret roughly inf_H {sqrt(T H log K)+Gamma_T(H)} plus meta-overhead and T/K.
ideas.title: Adaptive Truncation Oracle Bound
ideas.why_promising: The current sufficiency theorem needs a chosen H or tail rate. An adaptive skipping result would give a stronger positive theorem aligned with the modern delayed-feedback literature on skipped or outstanding observations.

ideas.risks: A broad modulus may become tautological or noncomputable. Same-prefix action laws fail for process-aware horizon-aware learners, and outside-surplus compensation can erase local gaps.
ideas.summary: Define a probability-weighted information obstruction, e.g. Exposure_T = sup over common-prefix events/candidate horizons of p|I|kappa_I - B, where B caps outside-prefix surplus. Prove the conditional transfer lemma gives lower bounds in universal or horizon-oblivious regimes, then test against sparse spikes, coded delays, rare events, and equal-revenue blocks.
ideas.title: Decision-Relevant Tail Modulus
ideas.why_promising: It targets the real obstruction identified by the notes: frequency, unpredictability, payoff relevance, and inability to compensate, rather than raw delay length.

ideas.risks: Mostly technical and may not create new mathematics; losses can grow with m if thresholds are close or if diagonal menus are mishandled.
ideas.summary: Create a reusable strict-crossing cleanup lemma: replace left-limit quotes a up to c_i by actual quotes c_i-eta_i, quantify the loss in N-block and multi-block theorems, and state exactly when sup comparators remove the need for eta. Include finite-grid versus continuum action-domain conversions.
ideas.title: Strict-Crossing Cleanup Toolkit
ideas.why_promising: Many accepted lower bounds and the solver's primal formula rely on left limits. A clean technical package would reduce repeated caveats in the final writeup.

ideas.risks: Running maxima do not capture rewards of quotes posted after downward moves; multiplicities and single-fill interactions may require more state than a threshold set.
ideas.summary: Extend the same-path multi-threshold theorem beyond increasing blocks. For arbitrary threshold order, rewrite zero-block fill events through running maxima and derive the correct weighted or repeated-threshold kappa game. Identify whether nonmonotone blocks reduce to record values or create new local obstructions.
ideas.title: Nonmonotone Threshold Blocks
ideas.why_promising: Real known paths are not sorted threshold menus. This is a necessary step from block gadgets toward a deterministic-path anytime characterization.
